title: Capacity From Your Own Numbers
objective: Build a capacity note whose every input cites a pe1t1-006 (or re-run) measurement, compute copies needed for a stated peak, project 2x and 5x, and show one sensitivity that changes the conclusion.
whyThisMatters: The architecture curriculum's capacity task allows back-of-envelope inputs. This term does not. A replica count that does not cite a measured SLO-meeting RPS is a guess. Staff engineers sign capacity notes that can be audited back to a run.
evidence: A capacity note that lists each input (SLO-meeting RPS, p95, error rate, saturation signal) with a file or run id from pe1t1-006 or a re-run committed here
Shown arithmetic for required replicas or equivalent capacity at a stated peak of at least 2x the measured SLO-meeting load
A 2x and a 5x projection each naming which resource hits a stated limit first, using a per-request or per-second cost taken from earlier measurements
A sensitivity paragraph that doubles or halves one input and shows the recomputed replica or capacity number
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: Every input number in the capacity note cites a committed run file or log line from pe1t1-006 or a re-run in this task — no invented RPS or p95.
Required capacity for a peak of at least 2x the measured SLO-meeting load is computed with the formula written out (not only the final integer).
The 2x and 5x projections each name one resource and the measured per-request or per-second cost that makes that resource the first limit.
The sensitivity case changes one cited input by 2x or 0.5x and shows the new capacity number from the same formula.
